metadata.title: SPARC Horizon threat model and security architecture review — attestation, revision 2

parties.name: Risk-Sentinel
parties.remarks: The reviewing individual is identified by the verified signature on the commit that introduces this record, not by a name asserted inside it.

metadata.remarks: Supersedes assessment result 238d6c86-650c-4dcc-993b-994043a24eb0, which was attested earlier the same day and went stale within hours: #27 added a rule fixing what a signature is computed over, which trips this attestation's early-staleness trigger for a change to the canonicalisation rule. The superseded record is kept unmodified. Its recorded hash e99b1dc168370017894d5452ff50013e40c0f73d6e9e0d4eb97b5a47a2812147 identifies the revision of threat-model.md it actually reviewed; that revision lives in git history, which is an immutable store here because main requires verified signatures. Editing a superseded record would break the only link back to what was reviewed, so it is never edited.

import-ap.remarks: There is no separate assessment plan. The requirement, its scope and its evidencing method are set by docs/dev/issue_rules.md and phase item S0-17 in docs/dev/Implementation_plan.md, which is what this href names. Recorded plainly rather than inventing a plan document to satisfy the field.

results.title: Threat model and security architecture review of the design of record, revision 2
results.description: Re-review of docs/01 through docs/10 as of 2026-09-19, after the signing rule added by #27. Nine findings, TM-1 through TM-9, recorded in docs/compliance/threat-model.md. TM-9 is new in this revision and is the reason for it: a signature that fails on a document nobody tampered with, because typed OSCAL rewrites timestamps and JCS does not normalise string values. None of the nine is marked mitigated, which remains the correct result for a repository with no application code.

control-selections.description: Developer testing and evaluation — threat modeling and vulnerability analyses.

observations.title: Threat model re-reviewed and attested after the canonicalisation rule changed
observations.description: The threat model was re-reviewed against the design of record following #27, which fixed what a detached signature is computed over. The review added TM-9 and left the other eight findings standing. Decisions across the nine: one deferred as an open phase-0 decision (TM-4, the chain head has no anchor outside the writer's control), one accepted and inherited (TM-8, deployment), one accepted risk within TM-5, and the rest carried as requirements on the phases that build the affected component.

relevant-evidence.description: The threat model at revision 2, hashed in back-matter.
The attestation this supersedes, and the hash of the revision it reviewed.

observations.remarks: Expiry is 180 days from the review. It also goes stale early, before that date, on a change to the trust boundary, the evidence chain order, the signing or canonicalisation scheme, how roles are derived from documents, the isolation of what-if overlays, the federation's peer verification or UUID key grammar, or on the first release serving real projections to an Authorizing Official. That list is not decorative: the trigger for a canonicalisation change is what produced this revision, hours after the previous one was signed. Completing a phase is not a trigger — building what the model requires does not invalidate it, changing what it assumed does.
